hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: The June 11 60-day ceasefire MOU commits Iran to reopening the Strait but implementation is unverified, ceasefire violations have occurred repeatedly, Iran retains effective control of the chokepoint, and oil at $74.98 WTI signals the market prices only partial restoration — not a clean BROKEN status given ongoing structural uncertainty.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS-confirmed May 2026 CPI at 4.2 percent YoY accelerating from 3.8 percent in April with the Fed funds rate pinned at 3.50 to 3.75 percent — real rates deeply negative — and GDP at 2.0 percent with a weakening labour market confirms a textbook stagflation regime with no policy exit visible today.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: The Fed has formally listed AI as a top systemic risk and the $725B Big Tech capex forecast for 2026 is widening the gap between investment timing and revenue realisation, while revenue-per-dollar-invested data from Sequoia and McKinsey confirm monetisation still lags by years — elevated VIX today adds bubble-burst tail risk.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold has corrected from above $5,500 per ounce in January to $4,277 today — a drawdown exceeding 22 percent — and while structural support from central bank demand and fiscal debasement remains intact per S&P Global analysis, the depth of the correction and continued 10Y yield pressure at 4.463 percent materially impairs near-term price recovery.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: S&P Global confirms spot treatment charges fell to minus $70 per tonne in March 2026 signalling extreme concentrate tightness, visible inventories above 1.3 million tonnes add near-term price pressure but a cumulative 3 million tonne deficit projected by 2036 keeps the structural thesis firmly intact.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Uranium spot is bid at $77 to $80 per pound with Sprott confirming tight supply and rising long-term contract volumes, the DOE awarded $800M to build SMRs in Tennessee and Michigan, and IEA projects annual nuclear investment rising to $210B by the mid-2030s — the thesis is intact but spot price is below the prior $86 to $90 contract band reference.

ALAB.note: Record Q1 2026 revenue of $308.4M growing 93 percent YoY confirms the AI connectivity thesis is operationally intact, but at P/E 89 and Price-to-Sales 34.77x versus sector average of 7.02x with an F Zacks Value Score and intensifying competition from Marvell Teralynx T100 and Cisco — which tripled its hyperscaler AI infrastructure order outlook to $9B in FY2026 — the valuation drift from fundamentals has not resolved and the AVOID signal stands.

POWL.note: The data center electrical infrastructure thesis remains supported by the trillion-dollar capex buildout and power grid constraints blocking Microsoft $80B Azure backlog, but at P/E 42.77 with no new major contract catalyst disclosed and broader industrial de-rating risk from a stagflation environment, POWL stays at WATCH rather than upgrading.

MOD.note: Negative FCF of minus $101M is a disqualifying quality flag that has not resolved — in a higher-for-longer rate environment this structural cash burn creates refinancing risk and prevents meaningful re-rating regardless of data center thermal management demand tailwinds.

GFS.note: The CHIPS Act foundry thesis produces no new major contract catalyst today and GlobalFoundries continues to lag TSMC and Samsung on leading-edge nodes, keeping the thesis in a holding pattern with no near-term re-rating catalyst identified.

CRDO.note: CRDO delivered FY2026 revenue of $1.34B — up 205 percent — with earnings up 805 percent and FY2027 guidance projecting over 80 percent revenue growth including $600M-plus from optical products following the DustPhotonics acquisition in May 2026, with multiple analysts raising price targets to $250 to $290 post the June 1 Q4 report — thesis is intact and WATCH signal should be upgraded to INTACT.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 136.54 with only $750M FCF remains priced for absolute perfection — the thesis drift is that ARM is now a derivative AI infrastructure bet at a prohibitive multiple with no earnings catalyst or FCF inflection visible in the near term to justify the premium over more direct AI connectivity plays.

S.note: SentinelOne shares dropped 8 percent in late May after cutting 8 percent of its workforce to redirect capital toward AI, signalling genuine FCF improvement intent but also competitive pressure — the $268M FCF is real but the restructuring charge of $25M and employee morale risk in a contested cybersecurity market keeps this at WATCH.

ZS.note: Zscaler maintains the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1B but remains rated AVOID — the valuation at P/E 28.37 does not screen as expensive yet the growth deceleration thesis and intensifying platform competition have not resolved in ZS favor.

AXON.note: AXON at EV-to-EBITDA 379 with only $63M FCF represents complete thesis drift — the original law enforcement technology thesis has been overwhelmed by pure speculative expansion multiple inflation, and no new catalyst today closes the fundamental gap between price and intrinsic value.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
